header.running_head: Various Lectures that Hadhrat Umar (RA) Delivered

Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) left Mina (after his stay in Makkah), he sat his camel down at Abtah, where he made a mound with the loose sand. Thereafter, he cast a portion of his garment over the mound and then leaned against it. He then raised his hands and made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! I am growing old, my strength is dwindling and my subjects have all dispersed far and wide. Do call me to You while I am not guilty of sinning nor have I been negligent in any duty."
When Hadhrat Umar (RA) reached Madinah, he addressed the people saying, "O people! The Faraa'idh have been ordained for you, the Sunan have been shown to you and you have been left on a clear path." He then hit his right hand on the left and added, "Unless you sway people to the right and left and lead them astray. Beware that you never destroy yourselves because of the verse of Rajm and never let anyone say that we do not find two penalties in Allaah's Book (we find only the one for lashing a fornicator and not the one for stoning an adulterer). I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ having people stoned and we have also done so after him. Had it not been for people remarking that Umar adds new things to Allaah's book, I would have written in (a footnote of) the Qur'aan the verse that we used to recite (while the words of the verse were abrogated, the law still remained). It reads that if a married man or a married woman commits adultery, both must be stoned."
Hadhrat Sa'eed says, "The month of Dhul Hijjah had hardly passed by when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was stabbed (and then passed away)." [^2]

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Ma'daan bin Abu Talha Ya'muri
blocks.text:
Hadhrat Ma'daan bin Abu Talha Ya'muri reports that it was on a Friday that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once stood on the pulpit and praised Allaah. He then spoke of Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) before saying, "I have seen a dream that I feel means nothing other than the approach of my death. I saw that a red rooster twice pecked at me. When I related the dream to Asmaa bint Umais (RA), she informed me that a non-Arab will kill me. Although people now want me to appoint a successor, you must remember that Allaah will never destroy His Deen nor the role of vicegerency (on earth) for which He sent his Nabi ﷺ.
If anything happens to me suddenly, the consultative assembly (to decide which of them will be the Khalifah) shall comprise of six men with whom Rasulullaah ﷺ was pleased when he left this world. They are Uthmaan (RA), Ali (RA), Zubayr (RA), Talha (RA), Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) and Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA). You people must listen to and obey whichever of them you pledge allegiance to. I know well that some people will criticise this matter and these are the very ones against whom I personally fought for the sake of Islaam. (In doing so) They will be joining the ranks of the enemies of Allaah and the misguided Kuffaar (because they will be assisting the cause of these Kuffaar).
I am leaving behind nothing more important in my estimation than the matter of
Ahmad, Abu Ya'la and Abu Ubayd.
Maalik, Ibn Sa'd, Musaddad and Haakim, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.90).
